reviewMethod: Independent visual reading of all 32 question-paper pages and PDF pages 3–22 of the combined Ordinary Level scheme (general notes, annotation palette, the Paper 1 scale table on page 6 and every Paper 1 model solution and marking note). Each task boundary is the published scale, not a parser count.
sourceNotes: Candidates answer any five of Q1–6 (30 marks each) and any three of Q7–10 (50 marks each): 380 offered marks, 300 candidate marks. Every question is retained; no combined multi-question cards.

42 independently marked units. Shared scales keep their parts together: Q1(b)(i)–(ii) 10D, Q3(c)(i)–(ii) 10D, Q4(c)(i)–(iii) 10D, Q5(a)(ii)–(iii) 10D, Q6(a)(i)–(ii) 15C, Q7(a)(i)–(ii) 10D, Q8(a)(i)–(ii) 10D, Q8(b)(ii)–(iii) 10D, Q9(a)(i)–(ii) 5C, Q10(a)(i)–(ii) 10C and Q10(a)(iv)–(v) 10D. Q10(b)(i)–(ii) and Q10(c)(i)–(ii) share one cross-letter 10D scale.
Paper 1 bands from scheme page 6: 5B 0,2,5; 5C 0,2,3,5; 5D 0,2,3,4,5; 10C 0,4,7,10; 10D 0,3,5,8,10; 15C 0,5,11,15. These differ from the Higher Level bands.
The question booklet is LC003GLP100EV.pdf; its indexed scheme LC003GLP000EV.pdf is shared with Paper 2. All page references are PDF positions.

Diagrams and tables (Argand diagrams, k(x) and its three candidate derivative graphs, the bus timetable, tax table, sales axes, running table, walkway, slide co-ordinate diagram and number lines) are read from the attached original question pages; prompts quote the paper’s own wording.

Scheme text layers set some symbols as characters that do not match plain text (for example the h′(x) model line), so card rows quote only notes whose text layer matches the printed scheme; the scheme reader shows the full published notes.

cards.questionText: Sara pays for lunch for herself and a friend. Sara’s lunch costs €34·60 and her friend’s lunch costs €28·90. A service charge of 12% is then added on. Find the total cost of lunch, after the service charge has been added on.

cards.stem: David buys a car for €22 600. It depreciates (goes down in value) by 18% each year, compounded annually.
cards.questionText: (i) How much does the car depreciate by in the 1st year? (ii) Find the value of the car after 2 years.
solutionQuotes: One part correct and work of merit in the other part

cards.questionText: A machine was bought for €28 000. The value of the machine depreciated by k% each year for 2 years, where k ∈ ℝ. After 2 years, the machine was valued at €20 230. Using the following formula, or otherwise, work out the value of k, where F is the value of the machine after t years and P is the initial value of the machine: F = P(1 − k/100)^t
solutionQuotes: Work of merit, for example, some correct substitution or trial and improvement
